name: Jobs-to-Be-Done (JTBD) Switch and Forces Interview
phase: Customer Discovery and Problem Validation Tactics
hypothesis: We believe that [persona] switches away from [incumbent solution] primarily due to [catalyzing push/pull force]. We will verify this by interviewing 10 individuals who transitioned between solutions within the last 90 days, and consider it validated if ≥ 60% point to the exact same triggering event and emotional crisis point.

plan.label: Preparation
plan.text: Recruit ten people who switched in the last 90 days and build the four-force inquiry matrix.

plan.label: Execution
plan.text: Walk the arc - first thought, active looking, deciding, consuming - and ask what nearly stopped the purchase.

plan.label: Data collection
plan.text: Map the active forces on a matrix, keeping push mechanisms apart from feature wishlists.

planFull.label: Preparation
planFull.text: Recruit participants who recently switched products within the category. Construct an inquiry matrix covering the four core forces: Push of the Current Situation, Pull of the New Solution, Habit/Inertia, and Anxiety of Change.

planFull.label: Execution
planFull.text: Interrogate the chronological arc of the transition: First Thought, Active Looking, Deciding, and Consuming. Inquire: "Where were you when you decided the prior solution was untenable?" "What almost prevented you from finalizing the purchase?"

planFull.label: Data collection
planFull.text: Map the active forces onto a Cartesian matrix, separating push mechanisms from unvalidated feature wishlists.

warning.label: Post-Hoc Rationalization
warning.text: Buyers build coherent narratives for decisions that were emotional, impulsive or organisational.

warningFull: Consumers routinely construct coherent, rational narratives for purchasing decisions that were fundamentally driven by emotional, impulsive, or organizational impulses.

origin.title: Competing Against Luck: The Story of Innovation and Customer Choice
